text: A resistance of 40 $\Omega$ is connected to a source of alternating current rated 220 V, 50 Hz. Find the time taken by the current to change from its maximum value to the rms value :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=I_{0}\cos (ωt)$ say

$\Rightarrow$ At maximum $ωt_{1}=0$ or $t_{1}=0$

Then at rms value $I=I_{0}/\sqrt{2}$

$\Rightarrow ωt_{2}=π/4$

$\Rightarrow ω(t_{2}-t_{1})=π/4$

$\Delta t=\frac{π}{4ω}=\frac{πT}{4\times 2π}$

$=\frac{1}{400}s$ or 2.5 ms

text:
A plane electromagnetic wave travels in a medium of relative permeability 1.61 and relative permittivity 6.44. If magnitude of magnetic intensity is 4.5 $\times$ $10^{-2} Am^{-1}$ at a point, what will be the approximate magnitude of electric field intensity at that point?

(Given : Permeability of free space $μ_{0}$ = 4$π$ $\times$ $10^{-7} NA^{-2}$, speed of light in vacuum c = 3 $\times$ $10^{8} ms^{-1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
H = 4.5 $\times$ $10^{-2}$

So B = $μ_{0}μ_{r}$H

Thus $E=\frac{c}{n}B$ (where n $\Rightarrow$ refractive index)

So $E=\frac{3\times 10^{8}\times 4π\times 10^{-7}\times 1.61\times 4.5\times 10^{-2}}{\sqrt{1.61\times 6.44}}$

$E=8.48$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text:
0.056 kg of Nitrogen is enclosed in a vessel at a temperature of 127${}^{\circ }$C. The amount of heat required to double the speed of its molecules is $____________ k$ cal.

(Take R = 2 cal mole$^{-1} K^{-1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The vessel is closed, so the gas is heated at constant volume and the heat supplied is $Q=nC_{V}\Delta T$.

Molecular speed varies as $\sqrt{T}$ (since $v_{\text{rms}}=\sqrt{3RT/M}$), so doubling the speed needs four times the absolute temperature:

$T_{i}=127+273=400\text{K},T_{f}=4T_{i}=1600\text{K},\Delta T=1200\text{K}$

Moles of $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$: $n=\dfrac{56\text{g}}{28\text{g mol}^{-1}}=2$.

For a diatomic gas, $C_{V}=\dfrac{5}{2}R=\dfrac{5}{2}\times 2=5\text{cal mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.

$Q=nC_{V}\Delta T=2\times 5\times 1200=12000\text{cal}=12\text{kcal}$

Hence, the answer is 12.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text: Two identical thin biconvex lens of focal length 15 cm and refractive index 1.5 are in contact with each other. The space between the lenses is filled with a liquid of refractive index 1.25. The focal length of the combination is $__________ cm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{1}{f_{l}}=\left (\frac{μ_{e}}{μ_{m}}-1\right )\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

here $|R_{1}|=|R_{2}|=R$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{f_{l1}}=(1.5-1)\left (\frac{2}{R}\right )=\frac{1}{15}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{R}=\frac{1}{15}$ or $R=15$ cm

for the concave lens made up of liquid

$\frac{1}{f_{l2}}=(1.25-1)\left (-\frac{2}{R}\right )=-\frac{1}{30}$ cm

now for equivalent lens

$\frac{1}{f_{e}}=\frac{2}{f_{l1}}+\frac{1}{f_{l2}}$

$=\frac{2}{15}-\frac{1}{30}=\frac{3}{30}=\frac{1}{10}$

or $f_{e}=10$ cm
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text: Sodium light of wavelengths 650 nm and 655 nm is used to study diffraction at a single slit of aperture 0.5 mm. The distance between the slit and the screen is 2.0 m. The separation between the positions of the first maxima of diffraction pattern obtained in the two cases is $___________$ $\times$ $10^{-5} m$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Condition for diffraction maximum is $a\sin θ=(2n+1)\frac{π}{2}$

For first Maxima, $n=1,a\sin θ=\frac{3λ}{2}$ 

Since $θ$ is very less, so

$\begin{array}{l} \sin θ\approx \tan θ \\  \\ \therefore a\tan θ=\dfrac{3λ}{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} a\left (\dfrac{y}{D}\right )=\dfrac{3λ}{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow y=\dfrac{3λ\mathrm{D}}{2a} \end{array}$

For the two cases given

$\begin{array}{ll} y_{2}-y_{1} & =\dfrac{3\mathrm{D}}{2a}(λ_{2}-λ_{1}) \\  \\ =\dfrac{3}{2}\times \dfrac{2}{0\cdot 5\times 10^{-3}}(655-650)\times 10^{-9} \\  \\ =6\times 10^{3}\times 5\times 10^{-9} \\  \\ =3\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{m} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text: When light of frequency twice the threshold frequency is incident on the metal plate, the maximum velocity of emitted electron is $v_{1}$. solution.body:

$\Rightarrow 2𝜙=𝜙+\frac{1}{2}mv_{1}^{2}$ ...... (1)

and $5𝜙=𝜙+\frac{1}{2}mv_{2}^{2}$ ..... (2)

From (1) and (2)

$\frac{v_{2}^{2}}{v_{1}^{2}}=\frac{4}{1}$ or $\frac{v_{2}}{v_{1}}=2$

text: From the top of a tower, a ball is thrown vertically upward which reaches the ground in 6 s. A second ball thrown vertically downward from the same position with the same speed reaches the ground in 1.5 s. A third ball released, from the rest from the same location, will reach the ground in $____________ s$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Based on the situation

$h=-ut_{1}+\frac{1}{2}gt_{1}^{2}$ $\to$ throwing up ....... (i)

$h=ut_{2}+\frac{1}{2}gt_{2}^{2}$ $\to$ throwing down ....... (ii)

$h=\frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$ $\to$ dropping .......... (iii)

and $0=u(t_{1}-t_{2})-\frac{1}{2}g(t_{1}-t_{2})^{2}$ ....... (iv)

solving above equations

$t=\sqrt{t_{1}t_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow t=\sqrt{6\times 1.5}=3s$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text: A metre scale is balanced on a knife edge at its centre. When two coins, each of mass 10 g are put one on the top of the other at the 10.0 cm mark the scale is found to be balanced at 40.0 cm mark. The mass of the metre scale is found to be x $\times$ $10^{-2} kg$. The value of x is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Let $\mathrm{M}$ be the mass of the meter scale.

The weight $\mathrm{Mg}$ of the scale acts at $50\mathrm{cm}$ mark.

 Finally after putting two coins on the meter scale, balancing the torques about the knife edge, we get, 

$20g\times 30=\mathrm{Mg}\times 10$

$\begin{array}{ll} M & =60\mathrm{g} \\  \\ \quad =60\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{kg} \\  \\ \quad =6\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{kg} \\  \\ \quad =x\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{kg} \end{array}$

On comparing, we get $x=6$
